::: {.hero-bio}

I am a PhD candidate in Economics at Universitas Indonesia. My research is in
development economics, urban and regional economics, political economy, and
spatial economics, with an emphasis on causal inference and spatial empirical
methods. My current work asks how large natural shocks reshape social order and
household behaviour in Indonesian villages.

Alongside my academic work, I work extensively in Indonesian public procurement
as a certified facilitator, competency assessor, and advisor, with a focus on
procurement strategy, contract management, and the professionalisation of the
procurement workforce.

:::

## Selected research

:::: {.paper}

::: {.paper-title}

Motive Without Mobilization? Earthquakes and Communal Conflict in Indonesia

:::

::: {.paper-meta}

Job market paper &nbsp;·&nbsp; [Working paper]{.paper-status}

:::

::: {.paper-abstract}

Combining seven waves of Indonesia's Village Potential Survey (PODES, 2005–2024)
with village-level USGS ShakeMap intensities, we estimate that first exposure to
damage-level shaking reduces reported communal conflict by about 1.1 percentage
points against a 4.8 percent pre-exposure mean. On identical villages and waves,
theft rises by roughly six percentage points while communal violence does not.
The pattern is consistent with a large physical shock raising the incentive for
individual predation while degrading the capacity to organise collective violence.

:::

::: {.paper-links}

[Details](research.qmd) [Draft available on request]{.disabled}

:::: {.paper}

::: {.paper-title}

Faith after the Shock: Earthquakes, Religious Expenditure, and the Insurance
Value of Religion in Indonesia

:::

::: {.paper-meta}

[Work in progress]{.paper-status}

:::

::: {.paper-abstract}

Whether religion functions as informal insurance against uninsured risk is
usually tested on stated religiosity. This project instead uses household
expenditure in rupiah, combined with village-level earthquake exposure, to
separate the income effect from the club-good and coping channels.

:::

## Public procurement

I have worked in Indonesian public procurement since 2015, in government
procurement roles and, since 2018, as a national-level facilitator and assessor.
My professional focus is procurement strategy and planning, contract management,
and the development of procurement competency across the public sector.
